# Pesher Psalms Column 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 4QpPs (4Q171), Col. 4 | **Condition:** moderate to heavy damage

---

**4:1** "For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His faithful ones; they are preserved

**4:2** forever; but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off" (Psalm 37:28).

**4:3** Its interpretation concerns [...] the Teacher of Righteousness and those who do [...] His will.

**4:4** [...] He will not forsake them [...] and the seed of the wicked [...]

**4:5** shall be cut off forever.

**4:6** "The righteous shall inherit the land and dwell upon it

**4:7** forever" (Psalm 37:29).

**4:8** Its interpretation concerns [...] for a thousand generations [...]

**4:9** to them and to their seed shall belong all the inheritance of Adam,

**4:10** and to their seed forever.

**4:11** [...] the high mountain of Is[rael...].

**4:12** "The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to slay him.

**4:13** The LORD will not abandon him into his hand or let him be condemned when

**4:14** he is brought to trial" (Psalm 37:32-33).

**4:15** Its interpretation concerns the Wicked [Priest] who watched the [Teacher of Righteous]ness and sought

**4:16** to slay him [...] and the Torah which he sent to him. But God will not abandon him and will not

**4:17** [condemn him when] he is brought to trial. And God will repay him by giving him

**4:18** into the hand of the ruthless ones of the nations, to execute [judgment] upon him [...]

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering. "Saints" (EMET) vs. "faithful ones" (LOGOS) — adopted LOGOS, as chasidav means "faithful/loyal ones" and "saints" carries later Christian connotations. "Seed" retained (EMET) over LOGOS's "offspring" and PNEUMA's "children" — biblical and precise. "Inheritance of Adam" preserved literally — not "humanity" (PNEUMA), since Adam may be a proper name here. "Torah" retained as a loanword (EMET) rather than "law" (LOGOS) or "instruction" (PNEUMA) — the term carries unique authority in Qumran legal contexts. "Ruthless ones of the nations" consistent with Col. 2 ruling.*
